hedges.reason: This is the only listed Democratic Senate primary, so it is the closest expression of the hedge thesis. Crockett entered late against the party leadership's preferences. She runs a combative, anti-establishment, small-dollar and online-driven campaign. If base anger at party leadership decides 2026 Democratic primaries, it should lift her over the candidates the party and donors prefer. That same anger is what beats Stevens in Michigan.

This is a weaker, cross-party version of the same mechanism. A 2026 primary electorate hostile to incumbents and to leadership-favored candidates would help Paxton against the Senate-leadership-backed Cornyn. Primary turnout in both parties is driven by activist anger at 'the establishment'. That same climate makes Stevens' institutional and AIPAC/corporate backing a liability.

claims.reason: Stevens losing would mean the 2026 Democratic primary electorate punished the leadership-favored, big-donor candidate. The same activist mood, with high-intensity insurgent turnout, small-dollar money and a backlash against caution from Washington, would show up earlier in the Texas primary and favor Crockett's anti-establishment campaign over the donor-favored alternative. The link is loose: Stevens could lose to McMorrow's generational-change appeal rather than a left-populist one, and Texas votes in March, long before Michigan in August. So this is a correlation claim, not a mechanical one.
